questions.question: Identify the correct form of the sentence using inversion for emphasis. The committee had not considered the proposal until we submitted it.
options: Not until the committee considered the proposal we submitted it.
Until the committee considered the proposal we submitted it.
Not until did the committee consider the proposal we submitted it.
Not until the committee considered the proposal we had submitted it.
questions.answer: Not until the committee considered the proposal we submitted it.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a cleft sentence to highlight the location of the meeting?
options: It was in the conference room that we decided to postpone the meeting.
It was the conference room where we decided to postpone the meeting.
It was in the conference room which we decided to postpone the meeting.
It was the conference room that we decided to postpone the meeting.
questions.answer: It was in the conference room that we decided to postpone the meeting.

questions.question: Select the correct form of the sentence with the third conditional structure to express a hypothetical situation in the past.
options: If I had known about the deadline, I would have completed the report on time.
If I had known about the deadline, I would have completed the report earlier.
If I had known about the deadline, I would have completed the report.
If I had known about the deadline, I would complete the report.
questions.answer: If I had known about the deadline, I would have completed the report.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a formal recommendation.
options: The committee recommends that all members attend the meeting.
The committee recommends that all members attends the meeting.
The committee recommends that all members attending the meeting.
The committee recommends that all members is present at the meeting.
questions.answer: The committee recommends that all members attend the meeting.

questions.question: Identify the correct sentence with ellipsis, where the word 'they' is omitted but implied from context.
options: The team completed the project, and the manager praised them.
The team completed the project, and the manager praised them.
The team completed the project, and the manager praised it.
The team completed the project, and the manager praised its completion.
questions.answer: The team completed the project, and the manager praised them.
